concepts.label: node
concepts.gloss: A node is a forwarding or switching domain within the multi-layer topology that hosts termination, service-access, connection, adaptation, and switching-rule resources.
concepts.example: R2 is a node in the OTN-over-optical topology, hosting link termination points toward R1 and R3 and an OCh/OTU4 adaptation.

concepts.label: link-termination-point
concepts.gloss: A link-termination-point is a node-owned edge point at which a topology link terminates, identifying that link's attachment to the node.
concepts.example: nep-R1-R2 is the termination point on R1 for link-R1-R2.

concepts.label: transitional-link
concepts.gloss: A transitional link is an intra-node adaptation relation that maps traffic between layer protocols or multiplexing levels described by a layer-protocol qualifier.
concepts.example: At R1, the OTU4/ODU2 transitional link adapts an ODU2 client signal into an OTU4 server signal.

concepts.label: service-interface-point
concepts.gloss: A service-interface-point is a node-associated access point through which a client requests or consumes a connectivity service.
concepts.example: sip-A1-odu is the ODU service access point at A1 used as one endpoint of cs-a1a3-odu2.

concepts.label: connectivity-service
concepts.gloss: A connectivity-service is an end-to-end traffic-connectivity offering between service-interface-points, realized by connection endpoints and optionally governed by a protection group.
concepts.example: cs-a1a3-odu2 provides protected ODU2 connectivity from the SIP at A1 to the SIP at A3 and is protected by pgroup-a1a3.

concepts.label: layer-protocol-qualifier
concepts.gloss: A layer-protocol-qualifier specifies the client/server layer or multiplexing relationship applicable to a connectivity service and usable by an adaptation.
concepts.example: ODU0 into ODU2 identifies an ODU0 client carried within an ODU2 server for the relevant service adaptation.

concepts.label: node-rule-group
concepts.gloss: A node-rule-group is a node-local set of constraints or capabilities governing which termination points or signals may be switched or cross-connected within that node.
concepts.example: R2 cross-connect rule group defines the switching combinations permitted through node R2.

concepts.label: link
concepts.gloss: A link is a topology-level adjacency between nodes whose ends are represented by node-owned link-termination-points.
concepts.example: link-R1-R2 connects nodes R1 and R2 and terminates at their respective edge points, including nep-R1-R2 on R1.

concepts.label: topology
concepts.gloss: A topology is the containing multi-layer network view that organizes the domain's nodes and the links connecting them.
concepts.example: The OTN-over-optical domain is represented as one topology containing nodes R1–R4 and A1–A3 together with links such as link-R1-R2.

concepts.label: connection-end-point
concepts.gloss: A connection-end-point is a node-local endpoint of the connection construct that realizes a particular connectivity service inside the network.
concepts.example: cep-a1a3-R1 is the R1-side connection endpoint belonging to the realization of cs-a1a3-odu2.

concepts.label: media-channel
concepts.gloss: A media-channel is an individual optical channel, typically a wavelength or spectral allocation, carried over an optical multiplex section and transporting adapted client/server traffic.
concepts.example: och-lambda1-R1-R3 is the lambda1 optical channel from R1 toward R3, carried over the applicable OMS resources and transporting adapted OTN traffic.

concepts.label: media-channel-group
concepts.gloss: A media-channel-group is an optical multiplex section between nodes that aggregates multiple media channels for joint transport over an optical span.
concepts.example: oms-R1-R2 is the optical multiplex section between R1 and R2 that can aggregate channels such as lambda1.

concepts.label: signal-grade
concepts.gloss: A signal-grade is a classified optical-quality level, such as an OSNR grade, assigned to a specific media channel.
concepts.example: lambda1 has grade-A, indicating a high-OSNR quality classification for och-lambda1-R1-R3.

concepts.label: protection-group
concepts.gloss: A protection-group is a resilience construct that protects a connectivity service by coordinating working and protection realizations, such as a 1+1 pair.
concepts.example: pgroup-a1a3 protects cs-a1a3-odu2 with a working route R1-R3 and a concurrently available protection route R1-R4-R3.

concepts.label: x-vendor-7731
concepts.gloss: x-vendor-7731 is an opaque vendor-specific node attribute whose hexadecimal value has implementation-defined semantics not exposed by the standard model.
concepts.example: On node R2, x-vendor-7731 is present with the proprietary value 0x1A.
